description.value:
Frequency 1/round

Requirement You've drawn blood from your Marked quarry this turn

Loose a wide double-strike: make a Strike against the quarry as normal; each other creature adjacent to it takes your weapon's damage (no ability modifier added) in the same type as that hit, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC.

cinderfall.incomplete: An AoE-on-hit action with its own save-DC block — this class of "type": "action" card in this corpus carries no save/damage schema fields to hang a basic-save AoE off of (unlike a spell record); building it would mean authoring a bespoke action structure this corpus doesn't have a precedent for, on top of the Mark block. This hands the actor a wholly new usable action/reaction. Confirmed absent per two direct spot checks: Fighter's Double Slice only rule-encodes its minor non-agile penalty -- the actual "resolve two Strikes as one attack, combine damage" behavior is hardcoded PF2e system logic. Fighter's Reactive Strike is granted via a bare GrantItem whose trigger is likewise hardcoded system behavior tied to one specific compendium action UUID, not a generic rule-element hook. Any Waywarden card proposing an equivalent bespoke Strike-triggering or multi-Strike-resolving action inherits the same gap. The Waywarden's central subsystem, The Mark (classes.waywarden.json flags.cinderfall.terms[0]: "designate a creature as your quarry, gaining a growing bonus to track, target, and punish it specifically"), has zero Foundry-schema footprint anywhere in the corpus. classes.waywarden.json:65 itself carries "rules": []. No card anywhere grants a TokenMark effect (site/data/cards/abilities/, class-features/, feat-effects/ are all empty scaffold directories -- confirmed via ls, contents are .gitkeep only). Real pf2e's own equivalent mechanic (Ranger's Hunt Prey) is fully buildable and precedented, but that infrastructure (an action item + a TokenMark-carrying effect item) does not exist for Waywarden and is not one of the 56 files in scope for this draft. This card is blocked until a future pass authors the base Mark action/effect.
